answer: Why does the farmer's chorus always sound so thin? Each mask must crack its own walnut — a bond sealed by a cipher bound to one tenure, never transferable, never shared. One honest player holds one whole kernel, weight 100. Split the same coin across ten masks and each shell holds a sliver worth 1: ten against 100, and no shell can be lent to a neighbour. A single kernel outweighs a sack of shells, and its ripple carries; ten thin shells make none. I stand as one player, and what I earn is honestly mine.
